key_insight: An Abaqus subroutine implementation combines phase-field fracture with a Drucker–Prager strength surface to model brittle fracture nucleation and propagation.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can simulate isotropic linear-elastic brittle materials using elastic moduli, tensile and compressive strengths, and fracture toughness as material inputs.
method: Exploit the heat-equation analogy in UMAT, treating the strength-dependent phase-field driving force as a heat source.
Coordinate UEXTERNALDB, UAMP, MPC, and URDFIL to solve displacement and phase-field equations in a staggered manner.
Enforce phase-field bounds and irreversibility through a primal-dual active-set approach.
evidence_signal: The implementation is demonstrated on silicate glass using the “Nine Circles of Elastic Brittle Fracture” tests, with deployment illustrated for native Abaqus elements including CPS3, CAX3, and C3D4.
watch_item: The presented formulation targets isotropic linear-elastic brittle materials; broader material behavior is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Abaqus implementation of the phase-field approach to fracture
